clue.text: Wild excitations and thrills

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, all eleven letters

explanation.surface: Someone describing a rush of wild excitement and thrills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild excitations' reads as one noun phrase, and 'thrills' as a second noun; in fact 'thrills' is a verb and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To intoxicate someone figuratively is to exhilarate or excite them, a close synonym of the verb thrill.

clue.text: Prompts marksmen to find targets here, did you say?

indicators.note: asking whether you said it points to how something sounds when spoken rather than how it is written

parts.note: a marksman finds a target when it is lined up in the gun's sights

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether marksmen are prompted to find targets in a particular place.
explanation.walkthrough: A gun's sights are the aiming device; a target is 'in sights' when lined up, and the phrase is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite someone is to urge or stir them to act, a straightforward synonym of the verb prompt.

clue.text: Vietnamese festival that starts year offspring mostly accepted in irritable fashion

indicators.note: accepted means taken in as a member, so the shortened offspring word goes between the festival and the year letter
the festival that starts the year comes before the year letter

parts.note: Tet is the Vietnamese lunar New Year festival

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the offspring word loses its last letter

parts.note: a child is someone's offspring

explanation.surface: At Vietnam's new-year festival, a child is grudgingly let in, in a grumpy way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts CHILD to CHIL, which is 'accepted' between TET and Y. Tet really does start the Vietnamese year, which is why 'that starts' puts it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy means bad-tempered and touchy, so the adverb describes acting in an irritable fashion.

clue.text: Medical procedure that follows whiskey?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an image of the inside of the body taken with radiation
second meaning: the code word after Whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A joke that you'll need a scan after too much whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: The NATO alphabet runs Victor, Whiskey, then this word for X, then Yankee; the drink is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiograph is a common hospital examination, and the same code word stands for the letter X in radio spelling.

clue.text: Secret kind of trick

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word before 'trick' naming a swindle that wins a victim's trust

explanation.surface: A magician's hint that a certain sort of trick is secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secret' looks like an adjective describing the trick; it is a noun, one thing told in private.
explanation.definitionFit: A private disclosure is called a confidence, and a con trick is short for a scam built on gaining trust.

clue.text: Sound of disapproval twice at the outset, Everyman's one to be taught a lesson

definitions.text: one to be taught a lesson

parts.note: the clicking noise made to show mild disapproval

indicators.note: the outset of a word is where it begins, so its opening letter is taken

parts.note: the setter's name supplies its opening letter
the same letter a second time

explanation.surface: The setter, tut-tutting, promising to teach someone a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' makes it look as if the disapproving sound is doubled; it actually doubles the first letter of Everyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is a student who receives instruction from a tutor, someone being given lessons.

clue.text: Old rakes initially wearing smart clothes: they're after wives

indicators.note: whatever is worn goes around the wearer, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: formal matching jacket-and-trouser outfits

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives up its first letter

parts.note: opening letter
opening letter

explanation.surface: Elderly womanisers dressed up sharply, hunting for brides.
explanation.walkthrough: A rake is a dissolute man-about-town, which suits the picture of men chasing wives; here only the initials count.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitors are men courting a woman in hope of marriage, so they are pursuing future wives.

clue.text: Female relative, imperious, departs; merriment stifled at first

parts.note: grand in the sense of haughty and lordly is imperious
D is the abbreviation for departs, as on a timetable

indicators.note: stifled at first means cut off at the start, so the merriment word loses its opening letter

parts.note: laughter is merriment

explanation.surface: A haughty woman storms out, and the laughter dies away at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stifled at first' drops the L of LAUGHTER, leaving AUGHTER. D for departs is the railway timetable abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A granddaughter is the daughter of one's son or daughter, a female member of the family.

clue.text: Source of refreshment befuddled king and writer

indicators.note: a befuddled mind is muddled and confused, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: all thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk king and a writer, perhaps sharing the bottle together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Befuddled' suits drink in the surface, but the refreshment is clean water rather than alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Water fit for people to drink is what quenches thirst, the most basic thing that refreshes.

clue.text: Slice of Kashmiri cottage cheese

indicators.note: a slice is a piece cut from something larger, so the letters are a run taken from within the words

parts.note: runs from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A portion of cheese made in a Kashmiri cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cottage cheese' is a real cheese and wants to be the definition; the cottage only hides the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese, one particular example of the general category.

clue.text: After November, say, one's eaten more crackers

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece is put within another

parts.note: to utter is to say
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: After November, someone has eaten more Christmas crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' looks like food or festive crackers; here it is British slang for crazy. 'Say' looks like 'for example' but gives a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is informal British for mad, and nutty is a slang synonym, so the comparative forms match.

clue.text: Nick wanting direction, disheartened, embracing Conservatives' leader

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the reduced direction wraps around the leader letter
disheartened means with its heart taken out, so the middle letter of the direction goes

parts.note: north is a compass direction

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Conservatives'

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick, lost and dispirited, hugs the head of the Tories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' takes the middle R from NORTH to leave NOTH, which is 'embracing' C, the 'leader' of Conservatives'. 'Nick' tempts as a name, or as stealing, but means a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut in an edge or surface, which is what a nick is.

clue.text: Make music, sad and quiet

definitions.note: a verb here, as in 'to quiet down'

parts.note: to pipe is to play a pipe
feeling down is feeling sad

explanation.surface: A description of mournful, soft music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sad and quiet' reads as a pair of adjectives for the music; 'quiet' is actually a verb defining the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to stop talking or make less noise, an informal way of saying become silent.

clue.text: In a Nissan, the writer's on island somewhere in S Pacific

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Micra is a small Nissan car model
a writer may refer to themself as 'one', so the writer's is one's
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone driving a Nissan on an island in the South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second, so the writer's comes before island inside the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Micronesia is a region and nation of small islands in the western Pacific Ocean, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Record me in retreat: 'One denies responsibility'

definitions.note: a clause describing the answer, a statement in which one denies responsibility

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the pieces nest

parts.note: a lair is a hiding place or den to retreat to
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recording of someone in retreat, reading out a legal get-out line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' looks like a verb about withdrawing; it is the noun, a hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclaimer is a formal statement rejecting liability, which is literally a notice where the writer denies being answerable.

clue.text: It's a flipping sparkling wine

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark: it's a blasted fizzy wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' sounds like a mild British swear word, as in 'flipping heck'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sweet sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy, named after its home town.

clue.text: Time for quiet: pet dog becomes talking animal

indicators.note: one thing for another means in place of it, so a letter is swapped

parts.note: a cockapoo is a crossbreed of cocker spaniel and poodle
P is piano, the musical instruction for quiet
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Telling a noisy pet it's time to be quiet, as the dog starts to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time for quiet' reads as a call for silence; it tells you to swap the letter for quiet with the letter for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockatoos are crested parrots, and parrots are known for mimicking human speech.

clue.text: Compulsion to cleanse failing to start

indicators.note: failing to start means the opening letter does not appear, so the cleansing word loses its first letter

parts.note: to purge is to cleanse or rid of impurities

explanation.surface: Someone feels an urge to clean but cannot get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing to start' drops the P of PURGE. The surface suggests a lack of motivation, but the compulsion is the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a strong impulse or desire that is hard to resist, which is a compulsion.

clue.text: Grand old university buffet offering Hungarian stew

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
O is the abbreviation for old
U is the abbreviation for university
to buffet is to strike or lash

explanation.surface: A stately old college serving stew at its buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' wants to be a spread of food, which fits the stew; it is the verb meaning to batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Goulash is a paprika-spiced meat and vegetable dish, the national stew of Hungary.

clue.text: In advance, rustling up salad of rock pigeon

indicators.note: a salad is a tossed mixture, so these letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: all ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Preparing a pigeon salad ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rustling up' looks like the mixing signal; it is part of the definition, since rustling up a meal means cooking it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rustle up food is to prepare it, and doing so beforehand is cooking ahead of serving.

clue.text: Pick out one very good behind

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so is an intensifier like very, as in 'so good'
running behind time is running late

explanation.surface: Choosing one particularly fine backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' suggests a rear end; it means late, behind schedule. 'Very good' stands in for the intensifier, as 'so good' does.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate something is to single it out and separate it from the rest, a synonym of selecting it.

clue.text: Poignant, timeless article describing female relative

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing around, as a circle is described, so the shortened article goes around the relative
timeless means without time, and T is the abbreviation for time, so that letter goes

parts.note: an article in the sense of an object is a thing
an aunt is a female relative

explanation.surface: A moving, ageless piece of writing portrays a woman in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' takes T from THING to give HING, and 'describing' (in the geometric sense of drawing round) wraps it around AUNT. 'Article' looks like a piece of writing, but means an object.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haunting stays in the mind with a lingering, moving sadness, the sense of poignant.

clue.text: Newspaper X

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the London daily paper
second meaning: the multiplication sign, read aloud as this word

explanation.walkthrough: X suggests a letter or ten in Roman numerals; here it is the symbol for multiplying, as in 'three X four'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times is a British national daily paper, and the multiplication sign is spoken as that same word.

clue.text: King and queen on a Swedish coin

parts.note: K is king in chess notation
R for Regina, Latin for queen
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The royal couple pictured on a Swedish coin.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen, as on royal cyphers.
explanation.definitionFit: The krona is Sweden's unit of currency, and coins are issued in that denomination.

clue.text: Country. Habitable …? African desert, primarily!

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so each word gives only its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter
opening letter
opening letter
opening letter

explanation.surface: A puzzled note on a country: habitable? Mostly African desert!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both supplies the initials and describes the country, much of which lies in the Sahara.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked central African nation whose northern half is Sahara desert, barely habitable.

clue.text: Opera's musicians including Dutch thinker

indicators.note: to include is to contain within, so the letters lie inside the words

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An opera's orchestra featuring a philosopher from the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored when reading the letters across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was a Renaissance humanist scholar and philosopher, the most famous Dutch intellectual of his age.

clue.text: Boiling fruit for exciting social engagement

parts.note: boiling means very hot
the sweet fruit of a palm tree

explanation.surface: Stewing fruit ahead of a thrilling evening out.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words of the answer have a second sense: the romantic one is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot date is an informal term for a romantic outing with someone attractive, which is an exciting appointment.

clue.text: Fiancé and messy bo'sun bathed

indicators.note: messy means disordered, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: all eleven letters taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A bride's intended and a scruffy sailor who has just had a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: A bo'sun, or boatswain, is the ship's officer in charge of deck crew and rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiancé is a man engaged to be married, so he is the future spouse awaiting the wedding.
